task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 17, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style news update on employees' agreement to purchase Ospen Toolworks, explaining what has been agreed and how membership differs from simply keeping a job there.

facts.text: Ospen Toolworks' retiring owner, Halen Pike, signed a sale agreement with an employee cooperative on Monday, Aug. 17, 2026.
The planned ownership transfer is Oct. 1, subject to the lender's final equipment valuation.
Eighteen of the shop's 26 employees, a count excluding Pike, have agreed to become cooperative members.
Each founding member will contribute $5,000, producing $90,000 in member capital.
The $1 million purchase price will be funded by that $90,000, a $510,000 community-lender loan and $400,000 in seller financing.
A separate $250,000 working-capital facility is approved but is not part of the purchase price; the record does not state that any of it has been drawn.
The eight nonmember employees can remain in their current jobs at the same base pay and apply for membership later.
Member voting will be one person, one vote, rather than proportional to job title or years of service.
The cooperative's five-member board will appoint a general manager; daily production decisions will not require votes by all members.
The agreement retains Pike for six months as a paid adviser on customer relationships and quoting work.
Pike had explored a sale to a competitor that wanted the customer list but had made no written offer for the plant.
The shop makes small batches of replacement parts for food-processing equipment and water pumps.
Its largest customer supplied 28% of last year's revenue and has not committed to a new long-term contract.
Founding member Toma Wren said, "We are buying the responsibility for the next order, not a guarantee that it will come."
Nonmember machinist Iri Bell said the $5,000 contribution is beyond her current savings, although she wants the shop to remain open.
Bell said, "I can be glad the shop survives without being able to buy a piece of it this month."
The cooperative is considering installment payments for later members but has not adopted a policy.
The lender requires quarterly financial reports and has not promised to cover future operating losses.
The shop opened in 1987 and uses both computer-controlled lathes and an older manual milling machine.
The sale agreement does not guarantee permanent employment, dividends or a future resale value for membership shares.

All workers are owners or membership guarantees dividends and permanent jobs
